```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Most workflows can begin with [Getting started](getting-started.html), followed
by [category tables](tabulation.html) or
[measurement summaries](summary-statistics.html). This companion explains what
to expect when a result is a list, a group is missing, or a display shows only
some rows.

## Start with a tibble

This small illustration adapts the course survey, including a deliberately
missing centre to show how grouping works.

```{r survey, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidystata)

survey <- tibble(
  centre = c("Riverside", "Riverside", "Hilltop", NA),
  satisfied = c("Yes", NA, "No", "Yes"),
  score = c(2, NA, 6, 8)
)

survey |> tab(satisfied)
```

With tibble inputs, the `tab`, `summ`, `codebook` and `variables` families
return tibbles, including tables inside lists. Base data frames and data.table
inputs retain their respective table class where supported. Other subclasses
are not reconstructed on newly shaped tables; data.table summaries do not
retain keys or indexes.

`corr()`, `pwcorr()`, `spearman()`, `misstable()` and `duplicates_report()`
always return tibbles. Functions designed to return vectors, such as `ds()`
and `row_mean()`, still return vectors.

## Choose tables or lists deliberately

Separate one-way tabulations return a named list by default. Extract a table
by its name:

```{r list-result}
tables <- survey |> tab1(centre, satisfied)

tables[["satisfied"]]
```

To work with one tibble instead, combine the variable tables:

```{r combined-result}
survey |> tab1(centre, satisfied, .type = "tibble")
```

Output options vary by function:

| Option | Where it is useful |
|--------|--------------------|
| `"vector"` | The default vector of names from `ds()`. |
| `"list"` | Separate variable tables in `tab1()`/`fre1()`, or type families in summaries. A single summary family returns one table. |
| `"table"` | One table in the input's table class for `ds()`, `summ()` and `tabstat()`. |
| `"auto"` | Preserve the input's table class in `fre()`, `tab2()` and `fre2()`. |
| `"tibble"` | Explicit tibble output where supported; combines one-way variable tables or summary families. |
| `"flextable"` | Formatted output from supported tabulation functions, requiring the optional flextable package. |

`tab()` has no `.type` argument. Multiple-pair or explicitly grouped
`tab2()`/`fre2()` calls still return lists: `.type` controls each table
inside. Correlations use `.wide` for layout; both layouts are tibbles.

## Separate grouping keys from measurements

A missing centre is still a group, and does not make its observed response
invalid:

```{r groups}
survey |> tab(satisfied, .by = centre)
```

The one-way/joint tabulation and summary families inherit `group_by()` groups
unless `.by` replaces them. Their results are ungrouped.
Cross-tabulations require an explicit `.by` to split by group.

In summaries, `.missing = FALSE` drops missing grouping keys. Numeric
calculations always omit missing measured values. Tabulation percentages use
a 0-100 scale, while summary `valid_pct` uses 0-1. The dedicated
[tab](tabulation.html) and [summ](summary-statistics.html) articles demonstrate
the denominators.

## Handle empty and all-missing measurements

An empty input and an all-missing measurement have no observed values.
They retain `n = 0` and undefined statistics, including `sum = NA`:

```{r empty}
survey |>
  slice_head(n = 0) |>
  summ(score, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean"))
```

Entirely missing summary columns emit a warning. A row sum follows a different
convention: adding no observed items gives zero. A row mean stays missing.

```{r missing-row}
tibble(item1 = c(NA_real_, 4), item2 = c(NA_real_, 6)) |>
  mutate(
    total = row_sum(pick(starts_with("item"))),
    average = row_mean(pick(starts_with("item")))
  )
```

Empty selections produce empty tabulation results; row helpers need at least
one column. Matrix columns are unsupported by tabulation and column summaries.

## Understand labels and special missing values

Variable labels describe columns; value labels describe particular codes.
An SPSS-style export might distinguish a refusal from an unanswered question:

```{r labels}
imported <- tibble(
  answer = haven::labelled_spss(
    c(1, 2, 99, NA),
    labels = c(Yes = 1, No = 2, Refused = 99),
    na_values = 99,
    label = "Course satisfaction"
  )
)

imported |> fre(answer)
```

Tabulations recognise ordinary, tagged and SPSS user-missing values as missing.
Numeric summaries exclude them from calculations. `decode()` reads value
labels, but does not itself turn every labelled refusal into ordinary `NA`.
For calculations outside haven-aware functions, explicitly normalise special
missing values with `haven::zap_missing()`.

`misstable()` also accepts matrix and nested data-frame columns. Ordinary list
columns count scalar `NA` elements as missing and `NULL` as observed.
Structured columns use vctrs row-missingness rules; list-backed matrices have
different cell conventions, detailed in the
[missingness reference](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/misstable.html).

## Keep calendar units visible

When numeric and calendar measurements occur together, default summaries
separate the type families. Here the date table's SD retains duration units:

```{r calendar}
visits <- tibble(
  score = c(4, 8),
  day = readr::parse_date(c("2026-09-01", "2026-09-03"))
)
separate <- visits |> summ(.stat = c("n", "mean", "sd"))

separate[["date"]]
```

The numeric table keeps numeric statistics. In combined `.type = "table"` or
`"tibble"` output, shared location columns become character. Spread columns
become plain numbers: days for dates and seconds for date-times, with units
shown in `type`.

## Preview a table without removing rows

A longer course register is easier to inspect at its beginning and end:

```{r preview}
register <- tibble(id = 1:12, points = (1:12)^2)
view <- register |> preview_headtail(n = 4)

view
```

The display budget is four data rows, with an omission marker between the
beginning and end. All twelve rows remain available for calculations:

```{r complete-data}
view |> summarise(participants = n(), total_points = sum(points))
```

For a view across the whole ordered register, use interval previews:

```{r interval}
register |> preview_interval(n = 4)
```

Sort first when position should represent a meaningful order.
`unpreview()` removes the persistent display setting. Supported dplyr/tidyr
operations carry preview settings forward while following their own grouping
and container rules.

`print_headtail()` and `print_interval()` print once and invisibly return the
complete input. Wrapping and unwrapping data.table inputs copies them; later
native data.table mutations follow ordinary reference semantics. If removing
source columns with `as_dummy(.remove = TRUE)` would leave a data.table with
rows but no columns, retain an identifier or another source column.
